chunks: And Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrated that he said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled: 'That which the judges err in regarding blood (diyah) or cutting (limbs), it is upon the treasury of the Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: Who bears the financial cost when judges make an error in criminal rulings?
ai.summary: Reported by Al-Asbagh ibn Nabata from Imam Ali (AS), this hadith establishes the principle of state liability for judicial errors (khata') in hudud and qisas cases, ensuring that the financial burden of mistaken amputations or blood money falls on the public treasury (bayt al-mal) rather than the accused or victim. This ruling underscores the accountability of the judiciary in Shia jurisprudence and reflects the early Islamic administration's commitment to justice and fiscal responsibility under the Caliphate.
